items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was featuring a tune composed by Henri Salvador, a French Martinque comedian and fine guitarist and singer.

ctx.x: I was featuring a tune composed by Henri Salvador, a French Martinque comedian and fine guitarist and singer. The song was "Une Chanson Douce" which was not meant to be and was not a jazz number, but it was a nice commercial number for dancers. About two weeks after I had started in the joint, I came in one night and this other orchestra, who always started playing before my group did were playing "Une Chanson Douce". I was salty as ocean water because my repertoire was not great as we had only a few rehearsals…

So when the night was finished, I told the leader of the band that I didn't like it and thought it was not fair for them to play that number when they knew it was one that I played and to play it before me. They didn't do it any more but the pianist got mad and never spoke to me again. And I'm still crying in my beer because of that, ha! ha!
